packages.title: Calendar: the landing preview without its duplicate task, and a return to today starts at the top
brief: Round 2 (b1). UX-1309 (S3) was partly fixed in round 1 and has failed once. What P169 built: (a) every landing waits for the save message and clears its measured height + 8 dp, with 88 dp only as the fallback (`App/lib/screens/calendar_screen.dart`, `_scrollToLit` about :183-195, `_messageClearance` :349-368); (b) the block from the first to the last lit row is revealed only when it fits (`lastEnd <= top`, :231), and otherwise the first lit row; (c) each lit row fades 1.5 s after it is seen whole above the message, and a row out of view stays lit until it's scrolled into view (`_watchLit` :286-323, `_scrolled` :275-282). Review B confirmed all three, and three renders pass.

Why it failed: acceptance 1 (ES, 1× on 360×800, both of today's lit rows above the message) can't hold with this fixture. The preview's `normalDay()` (`App/test/ux_previews/support/fixtures.dart:128`) already holds its own «Recoger a los niños del colegio» at 17:00 (id 4), and the three-task answer (`threeTasks()`, `App/test/ux_previews/capture_previews.dart:147-152`) adds the same title at 17:00. So «Llamar al médico para pedir cita», «Comer con Ana» and the old «Recoger…» sit between the two lit rows. Even with «Comprar pan y leche» pinned to the top, the block is 82 dp too tall at 360 dp and 6 dp too tall at 393 dp (measured by both the implementer and the tester). The code follows the brief; the check assumed a fixture that fits.

Settled here by the organizer: rule (b) stands as built, and UX-1309's app code doesn't change. A day doesn't hold the same task twice at the same time, so the duplicate is a fixture artifact. It also renders two identical 17:00 rows, one lit and one not. Do 1: in the `calendar/agenda.added` preview (`App/test/ux_previews/calendar_previews.dart`, the `'added'` preview at about :229-242), open the app with `normalDay().where((task) => task.id != 4).toList()` instead of `normalDay()`. Don't change `normalDay()` itself, which many other previews use, nor `threeTasks()`, which the capture result renders use. Re-render `calendar/agenda.added` (es 1×, es 2×, ca 2×, es 1×-393). In your notes, report the measurements at 360×800 1× and 393×852 1×: the height of the block from the top of «Comprar pan y leche»'s row to the bottom of the new «Recoger…» row, the room above the message, and which case `_scrollToLit` took. Whether a lit row below the fold should get a cue is the owner's question D11: build no cue.

UX-1628 (S2), regression R1B-1 from P169. `_comeBack` (`calendar_screen.dart:391-399`) selects today after 30 minutes or more away, or on a new day, but never touches `_scroll`. So the offset a landing's reveal left survives the switch, clamped to today's extent. At 2× that reveal scrolls the week strip and half of «Agenda de hoy» off the top, as in `calendar/agenda.added.es.light.2x.png`. The person comes back to today's rows with the week strip and the header out of view, and can't tell the day changed. P169's tests check `find.text(todayAgenda)`, which also finds a header that is built but scrolled off screen (evidence: inferred from code). Do 2: when `_comeBack` doesn't return early (the 30-minute or new-day case), add a post-frame callback that runs `_scroll.jumpTo(_scroll.position.minScrollExtent)` if `_scroll.hasClients`. Jump, never animate: the person wasn't looking. A short return (under 30 minutes, same day) keeps the scroll offset as now. No copy change.

For ux-tester: replace the two failing UX-1309 1× tests in `App/test/capture_landing_test.dart` (the `for (final still in [false, true])` pair at about :1123-1134) with acceptance 1 below: the same save, on the test's `normalDay()` minus id 4, at 393×852 1×. Keep the 2× tests, the (b) empty-day control and the (c) below-the-fold test as they are. Add the UX-1628 tests, which check the viewport rect, not just `find.text`.

Don't touch: `_scrollToLit`, `_watchLit` and the fade timings; the landing messages' copy; `_followToday` and the midnight timer; the week strip (P175); task rows and the counts line (P178); D9 (a short return still hands a picked day to the next capture).
acceptance: ES, 1× on 393×852, after saving the three-task fixture from Calendar on today, where today's day has no 17:00 «Recoger…» of its own (normalDay() minus id 4): «Comprar pan y leche» and the new «Recoger a los niños del colegio» (17:00) are both entirely above the save message. The same holds with animations off, where the reveal jumps.
Render `calendar/agenda.added.es.light.1x-393.png`: both new rows are lit above the message, and only one row is titled «Recoger a los niños del colegio».

ES, 2× on 360×800, the same save on the same day: «Comprar pan y leche» and its «Sin hora» line are entirely above the message; the new «Recoger…» is still lit 3 s later, and is no longer lit 2 s after it has been scrolled into view (P169's (c) test still passes).

ES, 2× on 360×800: after a landing on Friday that scrolled the agenda (offset above its minimum), the app goes to the background and resumes 31 minutes later. Today is selected, the agenda's scroll offset equals its minimum, and the «Agenda de hoy» header's rect lies entirely inside the agenda's viewport.
ES, 2× on 360×800: after a landing on today that scrolled the agenda, resuming after midnight shows the new day with the offset back at its minimum.
ES, 2× on 360×800: resuming 5 minutes after the Friday landing keeps Friday selected and the scroll offset unchanged.
P169's lifecycle tests still pass: 31 minutes gives today, 5 minutes keeps Friday, a picked day still reaches the next capture, and after midnight the app shows today.
deviceChecks: Phone, largest font: save a task for Friday at night, then reopen the app the next morning. The week strip and «Agenda de hoy» are at the top.
Phone, largest font, 360 dp: after the three-task dictation, «Comprar pan y leche» is lit above the message, and the 17:00 row is still lit when scrolled to.

packages.title: Capture result: every result spoken once, «Ver lo que dije» set apart; the microphone reason only when Android asks
brief: Round 2 (b1). UX-1308 (S2) was partly fixed in round 1 and has failed once. What P168 built: `_announce()` (`App/lib/screens/voice_task_screen.dart`, `_CaptureResultState._announce`, about :2666-2696) runs after the result's first frame. One task gives «{title}, {taskDayLine}»; several things that are all to add give `captureThingsToAdd(n)`; an open question's text is added at the end. Why it failed review A: every other result returns without announcing (`adding` is false, or `cards == 1` without a task). That covers a single change, delete or new-project card, a search, and a mixed task + change + delete result. With TalkBack this is the same «Listo… then silence» moment the finding is about.

Do 1, UX-1308. Keep the two existing cases exactly, and replace the `else return` with three rules. (a) One card that is a command: announce that card's headline exactly as shown. Read it from the screen rather than rebuilding it: in `App/lib/widgets/capture_command_cards.dart`, give the headline Text inside `_Header.build` (about :381-384) `key: const ValueKey('command-headline')`. In `_announce`, find the first widget with that key under the card's context (`_cards[view.command.id]?.currentContext`, visiting child elements) and use its `data`. Examples: ES «Se eliminará: Ir a la peluquería (…)», «Nuevo proyecto: {name}», «¿Cuál quieres cambiar?». When that headline is only the task's title (the update card's `_Header(text: shown.title)`, about :954-957), add the filled button's label after a comma, for example «Ir a la peluquería, Cambiar fecha». (b) Several cards that aren't all to add (mixed results, or several changes or deletions): announce the filled button's label as shown, for example «Añadir, cambiar y eliminar» (`commandAddChangeAndDelete`). Read it from the built button (key `save-drafts`, the first Text under it) instead of recomputing the label chain at about :3940-3975. (c) No filled button (a search, which is read-only): the first card's headline. In every case, add the open question's text at the end, as now. Send one announcement per arrival, add no new strings, and don't move the focus.

UX-1626 (S1), regression R1A-1 from P168. P168 moved «Ver lo que dije» (`reviewOriginal`; for typed words, «Texto original», `reviewOriginalText`) to the end of the scrolling cards: the `ExpansionTile` at about :4079-4094. On a one-task result it now sits 1 dp under the task's own «Más opciones» row (AUDIT `capture/result · one-task`), as an identical full-width row with a leading icon and a chevron. A newcomer reads it as a second option of that task (render `capture/result.one-task.es.light.1x.png`). Do 2: make it visibly secondary and outside the card. Set the title in `theme.textTheme.bodySmall` with `colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant`; colour the leading icon and the chevron `onSurfaceVariant` too (`iconColor`, `collapsedIconColor`, `textColor`, `collapsedTextColor`). Leave 16 dp between the last card's bottom edge and the row's top in both layouts: compact cards already carry 12 dp under them, so add 4 dp after compact cards and 16 dp after a single card. No divider. Keep the label, the expansion, the words (`SelectableText`) and a tap target at least 48 dp tall. This replaces the «8 dp above Ver lo que dije» in P171's UX-1311 line: P171 keeps these 16 dp.

UX-1627 (S1), regression R1A-2 from P166. In `_startRecording` (about :983-1001), `_microphoneGranted()` is read alongside `_speech.permission()`, and `_askingMic` is set as soon as the status says not granted while the request is unanswered. When the microphone is blocked, Android shows no dialog, but the bridge still answers through the activity callback (`App/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/example/agenda/NativeSpeechBridge.kt:85-94` and :348-358). So the status read can win, and «Permite el micrófono para dictar tus tareas. Solo escucha mientras dictas.» flashes in place of Listo, with no question on screen, before the blocked banner. That can happen each time the sheet opens by itself. Do 3: start a 300 ms Timer alongside the request, and set `_askingMic` only when it fires with the request still unanswered and the status read not granted. Cancel the timer when the request answers and in `dispose`. Before 300 ms the disabled Listo shows, as it did before the reason line existed. Keep: the status read running alongside the request (never awaited before it: the speed bar); the line clearing when the answer comes; `_microphoneGranted()` answering true on error. A real Android dialog stays up far longer than 300 ms, and a blocked answer arrives sooner (inferred from code; the emulator lane confirms). Make the `capture/sheet.mic-asking` preview pump past 300 ms before it shoots.

Tests: reason-line tests mock `flutter.baseflow.com/permissions/methods` `checkPermissionStatus` (0 = denied, 1 = granted) and hold the fake bridge's `permission()` open (P166's note). Update the existing UX-1305 tests that expect the line at once so they pump 300 ms first. Re-render `capture/result.one-task`, `capture/result.several`, `capture/sheet.mic-asking` and `commands/cards.*`.

Don't touch: the cards' contents and copy; the result's reveal (`_reveal`, `_revealAfter`); the footer and its gaps (P171); P166's blocked and denied banners and buttons; the free-dictations line; `captureMicrophoneWhy`'s copy.
acceptance: Semantics, ES, `commands/cards.delete` (one deletion card): exactly one announcement, equal to the card's headline text as rendered («Se eliminará: …» with the task's title and day); the focused node doesn't change.

Semantics, ES, `commands/cards.change` (one change card): one announcement «Ir a la peluquería, Cambiar fecha» (the title as the card shows it, then the filled button’s label); `commands/cards.project-new` alone: its headline «Nuevo proyecto: {name}»; `commands/cards.change-which`: «¿Cuál quieres cambiar?».
Semantics, ES, `commands/cards.mixed` (a task, a change and a deletion): one announcement that starts with «Añadir, cambiar y eliminar» and ends with the open question's text when a question is open.
P168's announcement tests still pass: one task gives the title and the date line; three tasks give «3 cosas para añadir»; an AM/PM result ends with the question.

ES, 1× on 360×800, a one-task result (`capture/result.one-task`): «Ver lo que dije» shows in bodySmall size, in onSurfaceVariant (text, icon and chevron). Its row's top is at least 16 dp below the bottom of «Más opciones», and AUDIT lists no «Gap under 8 dp» between them. Its tap target is at least 48 dp tall, and tapping it still shows the words.
ES, 1× on 360×800, a three-task result: «Ver lo que dije» sits 16 dp (±1) below the last card; a typed result shows «Texto original» in the same style.

ES, first start with the permission not granted (status mocked denied) and the bridge's request held open: at 200 ms the sheet shows no «Permite el micrófono para dictar tus tareas. Solo escucha mientras dictas.»; at 400 ms it shows that line in place of «Listo»; the line goes when the request answers.

ES, status mocked denied, and the bridge answers blocked 100 ms after the request: no frame between the start and the blocked banner shows «Permite el micrófono…». The banner «Para volver a dictar, abre Ajustes y toca Permisos › Micrófono › Permitir.» and the filled «Abrir Ajustes» show.
With the permission granted, no frame of the start shows the line (P166's test still passes).
The plain one-task dictation test still passes.
deviceChecks: Emulator lane, `permission-mic.blocked` (ES and CA, on-device and online paths): a screen recording from the sheet's opening shows no frame with «Permite el micrófono…» / «Permet el micròfon…» before the blocked banner.
Emulator lane, `permission-mic.dialog.es` at 1.0 and 2.0: the reason line still shows under Android's dialog.
Phone with TalkBack: «Borra el dentista del domingo» speaks «Se eliminará: …» once after Listo; a mixed dictation speaks «Añadir, cambiar y eliminar» once.

packages.title: Recovery: the code field's label sits on the border like the other fields
brief: Round 2 (b1). UX-1629 (S1), regression R1D-1 from P170. P170 set `floatingLabelBehavior: FloatingLabelBehavior.always` on the email field (`App/lib/screens/login_screen.dart`, about :570) and the password field (about :663-664), but not on the recovery code field (`account-recovery-code`, about :615-632, whose InputDecoration is at :623-626). In the recovery-sent state (render `auth/sign-in.recovery-sent.es.light.1x.png`), «Código de recuperación» sits inside its empty field, while «Nueva contraseña» sits on the border right under it: two identical controls look different. At 2× the 22-character code label, at body size inside the field, is the one label left exposed to the cut UX-1617 fixed for «Correo electrónico» (inferred; no 2× render of this state exists).
Do: add `floatingLabelBehavior: FloatingLabelBehavior.always,` to that InputDecoration. No copy change.

Previews: the `'recovery-sent'` preview in `App/test/ux_previews/auth_previews.dart` (about :121-134) renders only `es1`. Add `es2` and `ca2` (from `test/ux_previews/support/preview.dart`) and re-render.
Don't touch: the code field's keyboard, formatter, autofill and validator (P191 changes them once the server half lands); the sent line; Google first; D2's fold (P193).
acceptance: ES, 1× on 360×800, recovery-sent: «Código de recuperación» and «Nueva contraseña» both sit on their fields' borders, above the empty fields.
ES and CA, 2× on 360×800, recovery-sent: AUDIT lists no cut text for «Código de recuperación» / «Codi de recuperació» or «Nueva contraseña» / «Contrasenya nova».
The code field still accepts a 45-character `uid:token` value, and auth_gate_test.dart passes.
deviceChecks: Phone, largest font: on the recovery form, every field's label sits whole on its border.

decisions.question: UX-1309 (S3), what remains after round 2. When two tasks saved for the same day are far apart in it (for example one with no time and one at 17:00, with other tasks between them), only the first can be shown above the save message. The second stays lit further down, and nothing on screen says it is there. Should a lit row below the fold get a cue, such as a small line or arrow pointing down? That would be a new element, with new copy, on every such landing. Or is the save message's count enough («3 tareas añadidas · también el vie, 23 de oct»)?
decisions.recommendation: No cue (subtract first). The message already counts every saved task, a lit row stays lit until it's scrolled into view, and most dictations hold one task. P197 doesn't wait for this answer. If you want the cue, it becomes its own package, with copy from a reviewer.
